title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear portions and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
During pregnancy, it's essential to consume enough iron and folate to ensure the health of both mother and baby. Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports fetal development. However, choosing iron-and-folate-rich foods can be challenging. In this article, we'll introduce three simple and delicious recipes that combine iron with vitamin C, making it easy for pregnant women to get the necessary nutrients.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken and Spinach Bowl with Lemon
* 100g grilled chicken (iron: 1.5mg)
* 100g steamed spinach (iron: 2.5mg, vitamin C: 50mg)
* 1 lemon (vitamin C: 50mg)
* 1 bowl of white rice

Grilled chicken is an excellent source of heme iron, while steamed spinach is rich in non-heme iron and vitamin C. Lemon provides additional vitamin C, enhancing iron absorption. To ensure food safety, choose fresh chicken and cook it thoroughly.

## Recipe 2: Baked Salmon and Broccoli Bowl with Orange
* 100g baked salmon (iron: 1.2mg)
* 100g steamed broccoli (iron: 1.5mg, vitamin C: 100mg)
* 1 orange (vitamin C: 100mg)
* 1 bowl of white rice

Baked salmon is a good source of heme iron and omega-3 fatty acids, while steamed broccoli is rich in non-heme iron and vitamin C. Orange provides additional vitamin C, enhancing iron absorption. To ensure food safety, choose fresh salmon and cook it thoroughly.

## Recipe 3: Grilled Beef and Water Spinach Bowl with Cucumber
* 100g grilled beef (iron: 2.5mg)
* 100g steamed water spinach (iron: 2.5mg, vitamin C: 50mg)
* 1 cucumber (vitamin C: 20mg)
* 1 bowl of white rice

Grilled beef is an excellent source of heme iron, while steamed water spinach is rich in non-heme iron and vitamin C. Cucumber provides additional vitamin C, enhancing iron absorption. To ensure food safety, choose fresh beef and cook it thoroughly.

## Food Safety Notes
During pregnancy, it's crucial to prioritize food safety to avoid bacterial infections and other health issues. Choose fresh ingredients, cook food thoroughly, and avoid consuming raw or undercooked food.

## Conclusion
These three recipes provide the necessary iron and folate for pregnant women, combined with vitamin C to enhance iron absorption. Remember to prioritize food safety and choose fresh ingredients to ensure the health of both mother and baby. For more information on prenatal nutrition and recipes, visit our [meal planner](/planner) or [read more about this topic](/blog/topics).

## When to Seek Help
If you have any questions or concerns about prenatal nutrition or health, consult your doctor or a registered dietitian for personalized advice and support.
